text:
anya: FYI — our sample-app streaming e2e failed twice on CI this morning. Browser EventSource connection drops after ~6 chunks, python-sdk keeps receiving but final JSON is truncated. @kevin can you take a look?
kevin: thanks, repro steps? saw a couple similar notes but not exactly this combo.
anya: steps are in the tiny repro in /examples/sample-app/streaming. Run `npm run dev` then curl the local proxy with long streaming prompt. Intermittent, ~1 in 5 runs. Logs below.
anya: ```
[2026-03-23T09:12:11.234Z] sse: chunk seq=4 client=browser
[2026-03-23T09:12:11.438Z] sse: chunk seq=5 client=browser
[2026-03-23T09:12:11.439Z] sse: heartbeat empty chunk client=browser
[2026-03-23T09:12:11.440Z] sse: client disconnect (graceful) id=abc123
[2026-03-23T09:12:11.441Z] sse: last chunk seq=6 client=browser
[2026-03-23T09:12:11.442Z] parser WARN: out-of-order seq=6 expected=5
```
kevin: hmm parser taking empty chunk as EOF maybe? the browser emitted a heartbeat (empty data) which our JS sampleapp treats as stream end, while python-sdk tolerates it and waits for seq=6. That would explain truncated payload for browser.
tom: is the heartbeat coming from runtime or upstream proxy?
anya: looks like runtime -> we emit "\n" as keepalive when no tokens for 200ms. But proxy sometimes injects an extra CRLF when client disconnects -> two consecutive empty events.
sara: could be auth-refresh race too — if auth refresh triggers reconnect while heartbeats are inflight, the EventSource implementation in our browser sample triggers onerror->close path earlier. python's requests loop reassembles.
kevin: opened a tiny repro that simulates: EventSource receives empty line, then small token chunk, with a client abort in between. Browser parser code path: `if (data.trim() === '') { handleHeartbeat(); }` and elsewhere onnostream close we call finish(). We're finishing on a heartbeat when there's a concurrent disconnect.
kevin: quick patch idea: debounce heartbeats (50ms) and treat them as no-op for finalization, and also change reassembly to accept out-of-order by up to 1 seq gap if resume token matches.
anya: can we also add a small buffer in the sample-app client to reassemble partial JSON across chunk boundaries? sample-app is meant for onboarding so we should be forgiving.
kevin: agreed. adding buffer + tolerant seq check. PR #4321 with tests.
dev-bot: CI: ran 12/12 streaming e2e on patched branch, 2 flaky runs previously skipped.
sara: nice. can we add a unit for the auth refresh + heartbeat interleave? that's the only thing that reproduced locally consistently for me.
tom: also check SDK parity: node JS SDK has the same heartbeat logic, go and python differ. We should document in DX notes that EventSource semantics vary and recommend using the client-side helper in sample-app.
kevin: adding a note in README with recommended EventSource helper (auto-buffer + debounce) and a fallback to xhr-sse for older browsers.
anya: repro commands and minimal patch in the PR — I added a tiny harness that flips a random disconnect to catch the race.
kevin: merging tomorrow if no objections. leaving TODO: make runtime output explicit `:heartbeat` event instead of empty lines to make clients more deterministic.
anya: will follow up to file an infra ticket to change proxy behavior too. Thanks all :heart:
